analysis.evidence: Noah is the subject. כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים says that he acted according to everything God had commanded him. The closing כֵּן עָשָׂה, “so he did,” confirms that he carried out those instructions.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּעַשׂ נֹחַ, “and Noah did,” נֹחַ names the subject of וַיַּעַשׂ. The clause אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים identifies Noah as the one whom God commanded.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The אֲשֶׁר clause specifies what “all” includes. Noah acted according to all that God had commanded him, and כֵּן עָשָׂה confirms that he did so.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition כְּ (according to) + masculine singular absolute noun כֹל.

analysis.evidence: In כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים, “according to all that God commanded him,” אֲשֶׁר introduces the clause specifying what כֹל (“all”) includes.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In צִוָּה אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים, God is the subject and אֹתוֹ refers to Noah, the recipient of the command. Noah did everything God commanded him to do.
analysis.morphology: Piel perfect, third person masculine singular, without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In צִוָּה אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים, “God commanded him,” אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the masculine singular verb צִוָּה. The object אֹתוֹ refers to Noah, who carried out the command.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular agreement.

analysis.evidence: In כֵּן עָשָׂה, “so he did,” כֵּן points back to כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים and affirms that Noah acted exactly as God had commanded him.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb of manner with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כֵּן עָשָׂה, “so he did,” כֵּן points back to all that God commanded Noah. The closing verb confirms that Noah carried it out.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular
